terms.comment: Classically a measure, and in Quintilian and Martial a poetic metre or a verse (Lewis & Short); the unit of length is modern, used since the eighteenth century (Morgan–Owens). A kilometre is chīliometrum.

phrases.english: The wall is two metres high.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 247, 345, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. metric length: meter.
